text: Professional Overview: Pediatrics is an important secondary discipline of clinical medicine. It mainly studies the basic knowledge and skills related to the growth and development, disease prevention, disease diagnosis and treatment, and health care of children from the fetal stage to adolescence, providing high-quality medical services for children.Duration of study and Degree: The duration of study for undergraduate programs is generally five years. Upon graduation, students will be awarded a Bachelor of Medicine degree.Main disciplines: Basic medicine, clinical medicine, pediatrics, public health and preventive medicine, etc.Core courses: including Internal medicine, Surgery, Basic clinical skills, Pediatric Internal Medicine, Pediatric Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Cell Biology, Human Anatomy, Histology and Embryology, Child Health Care, etc.Professional directions: Currently, under pediatrics, some branch disciplines and characteristic professional directions have also developed, such as pediatric surgery, neonatal medicine, child health care medicine, perinatal medicine, and adolescent medicine, etc.Knowledge and ability requirements: Students need to master the basic knowledge and scientific methods related to medicine, understand the anatomical and physiological characteristics of children at different stages, as well as the causes, mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnosis and prevention and treatment principles of common and frequently-occurring diseases. At the same time, one should possess the ability to diagnose and treat various common and frequently-occurring diseases in internal medicine, surgery and gynecology, as well as strong capabilities in the diagnosis and treatment of pediatric diseases and the screening and diagnosis of common genetic and metabolic diseases in children.Career directions: Graduates mainly work in various medical institutions, health care organizations, and medical research units, engaging in pediatric clinical medical treatment, health care, teaching or research. Some graduates will also enter schools, communities and government agencies to engage in work related to children's health. In addition, the demand for pediatric science professionals from private clinics and family doctors is also gradually increasing.Employment prospects: According to the data, the number of graduates majoring in pediatrics from regular colleges and universities across the country is 2,000 to 2,500. There is a shortage of pediatricians nationwide, and the employment situation for graduates majoring in pediatrics is good. The national graduate employment rate maintained an upward trend in 2021-2022, increasing from 81% to 93%. However, in 2023, the employment rate slightly declined compared to the previous year, ranging from 82% to 87%. Overall, the employment rate was at a medium to high level.
